title: The efficacy and safety of preoperative glucocorticoid in herniorrhaphy: A systematic review and meta-analysis
author: Jun Watanabe
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.btxhnpj6

steps.title: Define Study Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish the parameters for study and participant selection to ensure a consistent dataset.

substeps.instruction: Include randomized individual controlled trials (RCTs), including full-text, abstracts, and unpublished data.
Exclude cross-over trials, cluster trials, and non-randomized trials.
Include adults aged >15 years scheduled for herniorrhaphy.
Exclude participants with daily systemic glucocorticoid use or known adverse reactions to glucocorticoids.
Include trials comparing intravenous preoperative glucocorticoid administration with placebo or usual care.
Allow co-interventions such as antibiotics, analgesics, and antiemetics, provided they are not part of the randomized treatment.

steps.title: Identify Outcome Measures
steps.instruction: Define the primary and secondary outcomes to be extracted from the identified studies.

substeps.instruction: Primary Outcomes: 1) Mean VAS/NRS pain score at postoperative day 0 (use last score if multiple; use pain at rest if both rest and activity are measured); 2) Rate of patients requiring rescue analgesics during postoperative stay; 3) Rate of patients vomiting within postoperative day 7.

Secondary Outcomes: 1) Mean VAS/NRS pain score at postoperative day 1 (use initial score if multiple; use pain at rest if both rest and activity are measured); 2) Length of postoperative stay; 3) Mean VAS/NRS fatigue score at postoperative day 1 (use initial score if multiple); 4) All author-defined adverse events.

steps.title: Conduct Literature and Registry Search
steps.instruction: Perform a comprehensive search for published and unpublished trials across multiple databases and registries.

substeps.instruction: Search electronic databases: Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), MEDLINE via Ovid (1966-present), and EMBASE (1988-present) using the specific search strategies detailed in Appendix 1.
Search clinical trial registers: ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Platform Search Portal (ICTRP) using the strategies in Appendix 2.
Check reference lists of all primary studies, review articles, and guidelines.
Contact authors of identified trials to find additional published or unpublished studies.
Translate non-English papers as necessary for full assessment.

steps.title: Screen and Select Studies
steps.instruction: Implement a two-stage screening process to identify eligible studies.

substeps.instruction: Two authors (JW and KR or TK) independently screen titles and abstracts, coding them as 'retrieve' or 'do not retrieve'.
Two authors (JW and KR or TK) independently screen the full text of retrieved studies to identify inclusions and record reasons for exclusion.
Resolve disagreements through discussion or consultation with a third author (KK).
Remove duplicates and collate multiple reports of the same study.
Document the process for a PRISMA flow diagram.

steps.title: Extract and Manage Data
steps.instruction: Systematically collect study characteristics and outcome data using a standardized form.

substeps.instruction: Pilot a standardized data collection form on at least one study.
Two authors (JW and KR or TK) independently extract study characteristics: design, number/location of centers, hernia surgery/anesthesia types, date, participant number, and mean age.
Two authors (JW and KR or TK) independently extract outcome data, noting any unusable reporting.
Resolve disagreements by consensus or via a third author (KK).
Transfer data from the collection form into Review Manager 4 (RevMan 4.4.1).

steps.title: Assess Risk of Bias
steps.instruction: Evaluate the quality of included studies using a standardized tool.

substeps.instruction: Two authors (JW and KR or TK) independently assess risk of bias using the Risk of Bias 2 tool.
Resolve disagreements through discussion or via a third author (KK).

steps.title: Analyze Treatment Effects and Heterogeneity
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analysis on the extracted data to determine the efficacy and safety of the intervention.

substeps.instruction: Analyze dichotomous data (rescue analgesics, vomiting) as risk ratios.
Analyze continuous data (pain, fatigue, hospital stays) as mean difference or standardized mean difference.
Summarize adverse events based on original article definitions (no meta-analysis for adverse events).
Evaluate statistical heterogeneity via forest plot visual inspection and the I2 statistic (0-40%: not important; 30-60%: moderate; 50-90%: substantial; 75-100%: considerable).
Perform Cochrane Chi2 test (Q-test) for I2, with P < 0.10 considered statistically significant.
If I2 > 50%, assess the reason for heterogeneity.

steps.title: Handle Missing Data and Statistics
steps.instruction: Apply specific protocols to address missing information to minimize bias.

substeps.instruction: Request missing data from original authors.
Perform intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis for dichotomous data where possible.
Do not impute missing continuous data (per Cochrane handbook); perform meta-analysis on available data.
Calculate standard deviation from standard error or p-value using the Altman method.
If authors are unreachable, calculate standard deviation using confidence intervals and t-values (Cochrane handbook or validated method) and verify via sensitivity analysis.

steps.title: Evaluate Reporting Bias and Synthesize Data
steps.instruction: Assess for publication bias and perform the final meta-analysis.

substeps.instruction: Search ClinicalTrials.gov and ICTRP for unpublished trials.
If >10 trials are pooled, create a funnel plot and use Egger's test (P < 0.05 indicates significant reporting bias).
Perform meta-analysis using Review Manager software (RevMan 5.4.1) using a random-effects model by default.

steps.title: Perform Subgroup and Sensitivity Analyses
steps.instruction: Conduct targeted analyses to test the robustness of the conclusions.

substeps.instruction: Perform subgroup analysis by: 1) Hernia type (inguinal vs. abdominal), 2) Surgical approach (open vs. laparoscopy), and 3) Steroid type (dexamethasone, betamethasone, triamcinolone, prednisolone, or fluorometholone).
Perform sensitivity analysis by: 1) Excluding studies using imputed statistics, and 2) Including only participants with complete data.
